results.controlIntent: a. Use internal system clocks to produce time stamps for audit records; and b. Record, for audit records, time stamps meeting [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] that use Coordinated Universal Time, have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time, or that include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: Both retrieved CloudTrail audit records for the churn-predictor-endpoint carry ISO 8601 timestamps with the 'Z' (UTC) suffix, directly satisfying AU-8.v3(b)'s requirement that timestamps use Coordinated Universal Time. Specifically: (1) CreateEndpoint event (id: d3bf3ab6-7e80-46d7-973e-940a8b62fd8b) timestamped '2025-12-01T11:00:00Z', and (2) UpdateEndpoint event (id: 4651790d-2d29-486b-956a-2364bd8f3f60) timestamped '2026-03-15T14:22:00Z'. Both are recorded to second-level granularity, which is the standard CloudTrail resolution and consistent with typical organization-defined granularity requirements. AU-8.v3(a) is addressed by the fact that AWS CloudTrail uses AWS-managed internal system clocks synchronized via the AWS Time Sync Service (NTP-backed), which is a well-established AWS platform guarantee. No timestamp anomalies, missing timestamps, or non-UTC offsets were observed in the evidence. Confidence is medium rather than high because: (a) no explicit organizational policy document defining the required granularity was retrieved, (b) no NTP/clock-sync configuration artifact was available to directly confirm AU-8.v3(a) compliance, and (c) only two event types were sampled — broader audit log coverage was not assessed.
gaps: No organizational policy document defining the required time-stamp granularity (e.g., seconds vs. milliseconds) was retrieved — human attestation needed to confirm the assignment value in AU-8.v3(b).

No explicit NTP or AWS Time Sync Service configuration artifact was available to directly evidence use of internal system clocks per AU-8.v3(a) — this relies on AWS platform-level guarantees rather than customer-controlled configuration.

Only CreateEndpoint and UpdateEndpoint event types were sampled; registry approval events and other audit record types were not present in the returned evidence, limiting coverage of the full audit trail.
